title: zazz-worker deployment diagram
description: zazz-worker is installed beside zazzled and only ever started by it, as child processes of the daemon on the same machine. For `zazz add` and `zazz test`, zazzled runs short-lived `zazz-worker compile` and `zazz-worker test` processes inside the OS sandbox; for `zazz call` and human runs it keeps `zazz-worker serve` processes warm, one per pool key (script, caller directory, effective policy), each talking to the daemon over a socketpair on fd 3 and reading its precompiled module from fd 4. A script's guest reads and writes the caller's own streams, passed with each call. Only scripts whose signer is trusted with network reach HTTPS hosts. The macOS release ships it as a universal binary signed with entitlements for executable memory; the Linux tarballs and the Homebrew formula carry it too; delivery is recorded in macos/release/.dev.

nodes.name: Developer's machine
nodes.description: A Mac or a Linux machine with zazzled and zazz-worker installed side by side.

nodes.name: zazzled serve process
nodes.description: The daemon: its zazz module starts every zazz-worker process and owns the script registry.

nodes.name: Caller's zazz or zazzle process
nodes.description: The invoker that asked for the call and passed its standard streams to the daemon; over MCP there is none and zazzled passes pipes it reads instead.

nodes.name: zazz-worker serve process
nodes.description: One per warm pool entry: started in the caller's directory with an empty environment, standard streams on /dev/null, a new session and no core dumps; one fresh instance per call; kept idle for up to 60 s or 1000 calls, then killed.

nodes.name: zazz-worker compile process
nodes.description: Short-lived, inside the OS sandbox with an empty environment: reads a WASM module on stdin and writes the precompiled module on stdout.

nodes.name: zazz-worker test process
nodes.description: Short-lived, inside the OS sandbox with an empty environment: runs a script's test module against a scratch directory, snapshots and a replay file, and prints a JSON report.
nodes.condition: `zazz add` and `zazz test`, for scripts with tests

nodes.name: Script registry
nodes.description: $ZAZZ_STORE, by default ~/.zazzle/v1/zazz (mode 0700): the .wasm and precompiled .cwasm of every registered script, metadata, names, locks and scratch directories.

nodes.name: HTTPS hosts
nodes.description: Hosts on the effective allowlist, reached over HTTPS only, without redirects.
nodes.condition: A script signed by an authority trusted here with network, and asking for it in its manifest

artifacts.name: zazz-worker
artifacts.description: The release build, found by zazzled beside its own executable (or at $ZAZZ_WORKER); universal on macOS (lipo of arm64 and x86_64), per architecture in the Linux tarballs, installed into the Homebrew formula's bin.

artifacts.name: zazz-worker.plist
artifacts.description: Hardened-runtime entitlements (JIT and unsigned executable memory) applied when the macOS binary is signed, because wasmtime maps compiled code executable.

relationships.description: As long as the pool keeps it.
Starts it through the sandbox command with an argument list; WASM in on stdin, precompiled module back on stdout, with a time limit.
Starts it through the sandbox command with the test module, --cwd, limits and optional --snapshots, --update and --http-replay; reads the JSON report from stdout.

Unix socketpair on fd 3: u32 little-endian length plus JSON frames; a hello with the preopens, network policy and limits first (answered by ready), then one message per call with the three stdio descriptors attached (SCM_RIGHTS); progress and the result come back; cancel and shutdown end work.
Writes modules and metadata at add; opens the script's .cwasm and passes it to a serve worker as fd 4.
The guest's stdin, stdout and stderr are the caller's descriptors (or zazzled's pipes), received with each call.
HTTPS through ureq, checked against the allowlist per request, bounded by the call's remaining time and a 16 MiB body.
